newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers baulk at strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers baulk at strong dollar.

text.p: German cotton consumers have put off purchases because of high mark prices resulting from the firm dollar, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
Upland sellers were offering a wide range of varieties for shipment through first half 1998, it said.
Underlying demand was high and yarn prices had increased, but buyers were still awaiting lower raw cotton prices and spot markets were therefore very quiet.
Cotton stocks as of March 7 totalled 40,589 bales, up from 34,742 a fortnight earlier, but well below the 113,375 recorded a year earlier.

In the long staple sector, the Exchange reported trades in Egyptian Giza 70/77 and Giza 85 for 1997, Sudan Barakat and Central Asians for second quarter 1997 and U.S. and Israel Pima through first quarter 1998.
